title: Outset Medical Tablo Hemodialysis (HD) Machine - System Will Not Start or Fails Automated Setup
description: Troubleshoot startup, boot, or automated setup failures caused by power, connections, consumables, configuration, or environmental conditions before escalating for service.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Dialysis Continuity
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot an unreliable Tablo while a patient depends on it for treatment. If the failure occurs before treatment, keep the machine unavailable until it completes setup successfully. If it occurs during treatment, follow the facility's clinical procedure for safely maintaining or transferring therapy using another verified dialysis system. Inspect for smoke, unusual odor, fluid intrusion, abnormal heat, damaged power components, or other obvious hazards. Expected outcome: The patient is supported by a safe alternative when necessary, and troubleshooting proceeds only on equipment that is not actively supporting the patient. Stop immediately and remove the machine from service if a safety hazard is present.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Startup or Setup Failure
steps.instructions: Attempt a normal startup only when safe. Determine whether the system: Shows no signs of power Begins booting but stops Restarts repeatedly Reaches the user interface but will not begin automated setup Starts setup but stops at a repeatable point Displays a specific message or alarm Record the exact displayed wording rather than paraphrasing it. Expected outcome: The failure is reproducible and clearly defined. If the system now starts and completes setup normally, verify basic operation and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 3. Verify AC Power
steps.instructions: Confirm the power cord is fully seated and visually intact. Check the receptacle for damage or looseness and verify the outlet using an approved method consistent with facility practice. Avoid extension cords, questionable adapters, or unapproved power strips. Expected outcome: Reliable facility AC power is available and the Tablo powers normally. If restoring proper AC power resolves the condition and setup completes successfully, troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect External Connections and Machine Condition
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible external cables, connectors, doors, covers, fluid connections, and attached accessories for incomplete seating, physical damage, contamination, or obstruction. Confirm nothing is pinched, disconnected, improperly installed, or preventing normal setup. Expected outcome: All externally accessible components required for startup are secure and undamaged. Correcting an obvious external connection problem should allow setup to proceed.

steps.title: 5. Verify Required Consumables and Setup Components
steps.instructions: Confirm the correct dialysis disposables and other required setup components are present, properly installed, and compatible with the machine. Look for packaging material, incomplete installation, kinks, misrouting, or improperly seated components. Do not bypass a setup check simply to make the machine proceed. Expected outcome: Required consumables and components are installed correctly and recognized. If setup completes after correcting installation, troubleshooting can stop after functional verification.

steps.title: 6. Check Water Supply and Drain Availability
steps.instructions: Because automated setup depends on the machine's fluid preparation systems, verify that the approved water connection and drainage arrangement are available, connected, unobstructed, and appropriate for normal operation. Look for closed valves, kinked hoses, disconnected fittings, visible leaks, or drainage backup. Expected outcome: Water supply and drainage conditions support normal setup. If correcting an external water or drain issue allows automated setup to complete, the issue is resolved.

steps.title: 7. Verify Controls, Configuration, and Environment
steps.instructions: Confirm the system is being started through the normal operator interface without stuck controls or unintended input. Check for obvious environmental problems such as blocked ventilation, excessive heat, condensation, or recent relocation that may have disturbed connections. Do not enter restricted service modes or make undocumented configuration changes. Expected outcome: The machine operates in an appropriate environment with normal controls and configuration. If startup and setup now complete normally, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 8. Perform a Controlled Restart When Appropriate
steps.instructions: If no active patient is connected and no safety condition exists, perform a normal shutdown and restart using the approved user-accessible controls. Do not repeatedly power-cycle a machine that continually fails at the same point. Expected outcome: The Tablo boots and completes automated setup without recurring interruption. A successful restart followed by normal setup indicates the immediate problem is resolved.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After corrective action, allow the machine to complete its normal automated setup and required pre-treatment checks. Confirm that no unresolved alarms remain and that the machine reaches the expected ready state. Do not return a dialysis machine to service solely because the display turns on. Expected outcome: The Tablo completes startup and automated setup normally with no recurring fault. Troubleshooting can stop and the machine may be returned to service according to facility procedure.

steps.title: 10. Escalate a Repeatable Startup or Setup Failure
steps.instructions: If the machine still fails to start, repeatedly restarts, or cannot complete automated setup after external causes have been ruled out, discontinue further external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The device is removed from service and routed for qualified evaluation rather than subjected to unnecessary disassembly or speculative repair.

CCR.Complaint: Dialysis staff reported the Tablo powered on but repeatedly stopped during automated setup and could not be prepared for treatment.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the facility water inlet connection was not fully seated, preventing normal setup from completing.
CCR.Resolution: Reseated and inspected the water connection, repeated automated setup successfully, verified normal operation with no recurring alarms, and returned the unit to service.

title: Outset Medical Tablo Hemodialysis (HD) Machine - Water Inlet, Purification, or Integrated RO Problem
description: Troubleshoot water-supply and integrated purification problems caused by inlet supply, hoses, drainage, connections, environmental conditions, or service-level water-system faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Therapy
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot unreliable water purification while a patient depends on the Tablo for dialysis. If water quality or purification performance is uncertain, do not initiate treatment. If the issue develops during treatment, follow the facility's clinical procedure for safely maintaining or transferring therapy. Treat visible leaks, unusual odors, overheating, or suspected contamination as removal-from-service conditions. Expected outcome: No patient relies on a machine with uncertain water preparation, and unsafe conditions are isolated immediately.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Water Problem
steps.instructions: Determine exactly what staff observed: No water entering the machine Setup stopping during water preparation Repeated purification-related alarm or message Inadequate or interrupted water supply Drain-related backup Visible external leak Failure that occurs only in one room or connection point Record the exact displayed message if present. Expected outcome: The complaint is clearly reproduced and narrowed to inlet supply, drainage, connection, or machine-side purification behavior.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Facility Water Source
steps.instructions: Confirm the machine is connected to the intended approved water source. Inspect the accessible supply valve and connection for proper position, secure attachment, visible damage, or leakage. Do not modify plumbing or connect the machine to an unapproved water source. Expected outcome: An appropriate water source is available and connected correctly. If restoring the intended supply resolves the problem, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Water Inlet Hose and Connections
steps.instructions: Trace the accessible water inlet path. Look for: Kinks Crushing Loose fittings Damaged connectors Incorrect routing Visible leakage Debris or obvious external obstruction Do not disassemble internal water-treatment components. Expected outcome: The inlet path is physically intact and unobstructed. Correcting a kink or loose external connection should restore normal water intake.

steps.title: 5. Check Drainage
steps.instructions: Verify the drain hose is properly positioned and not kinked, submerged improperly, pinched, blocked, or backing up. A drainage problem can interrupt setup or purification even when inlet water is available. Expected outcome: Wastewater can drain normally without restriction or backup. If correcting drainage allows the machine to resume normal purification, the issue is resolved.

steps.title: 6. Compare the Location With a Known-Good Installation
steps.instructions: When practical, determine whether another compatible Tablo operates normally from the same approved utility area, or whether the affected machine operates differently when connected at another approved location. Do not move or reconnect equipment in a way that violates facility water-quality procedures. Expected outcome: The comparison helps distinguish a facility water or drain issue from a machine-specific problem. A location-dependent failure should be referred to the appropriate facilities or water-management resource.

steps.title: 7. Check External Environmental Conditions
steps.instructions: Inspect for recent plumbing work, loss of building water, unusual inlet conditions, freezing, heat exposure, recent relocation, or other environmental changes that may affect water delivery. Coordinate with facilities personnel when the problem appears infrastructure-related. Expected outcome: External infrastructure conditions are normal or an infrastructure cause is identified and corrected.

steps.title: 8. Repeat the Normal Setup or Water Preparation Sequence
steps.instructions: With the machine off patient and external conditions corrected, perform the normal accessible setup sequence. Do not override alarms or bypass purification-related checks. Expected outcome: Water preparation completes normally and the machine proceeds through setup. If it does, troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 9. Verify Stable Operation
steps.instructions: Confirm the machine remains free of water-related alarms or leaks and completes the normal pre-treatment preparation sequence. Inspect the surrounding floor and accessible fittings after operation. Expected outcome: Water inlet, purification, and drainage functions remain stable with no visible leak or recurring alarm.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Purification Failure
steps.instructions: If supply and drainage conditions are satisfactory but the machine cannot complete its water-preparation process, stop troubleshooting externally. Expected outcome: The unit is removed from service for qualified evaluation of the integrated purification system or related internal controls.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported the Tablo repeatedly stopped during water preparation and would not complete setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external inlet hose sharply kinked behind the machine, restricting water flow.
CCR.Resolution: Corrected the hose routing, inspected the connections for leaks, repeated setup successfully, and verified normal water preparation before returning the unit to service.

helpfulDetails: Results at another approved connection point

title: Outset Medical Tablo Hemodialysis (HD) Machine - Conductivity Out of Range or Dialysate Will Not Stabilize
description: Troubleshoot unstable dialysate conductivity by checking concentrates, water preparation, consumables, connections, setup, and external conditions before service escalation.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient
steps.instructions: Do not continue dialysis when dialysate conductivity is unreliable or outside the machine's accepted operating condition. If the issue occurs during treatment, follow the facility's clinical procedure for safely stopping, maintaining, or transferring therapy. Never bypass a conductivity alarm. Expected outcome: The patient is not exposed to dialysate of uncertain composition, and the affected machine is available for off-patient troubleshooting.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Conductivity Complaint
steps.instructions: Determine whether conductivity: Fails to stabilize during setup Drifts after initially stabilizing Produces a repeated warning or alarm Changes after a concentrate or consumable change Occurs only at one location or water connection Record exact messages and the point in the sequence where the condition appears. Expected outcome: The failure pattern is documented and reproducible.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Correct Concentrates and Consumables
steps.instructions: Confirm that all required concentrates and disposable components are the correct type for the intended treatment and are installed according to normal clinical setup. Inspect labels, connections, expiration status when applicable, and obvious container damage or contamination. Do not substitute products that are not approved for the system. Expected outcome: Correct supplies are present and properly connected. If an incorrect or improperly connected supply is corrected and conductivity stabilizes, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Concentrate Connections and Fluid Paths
steps.instructions: Check accessible concentrate connections for: Loose fittings Kinks Pinched tubing Empty or inadequately supplied containers Air entering through an improperly seated connection Visible leakage Avoid opening internal fluid-path components. Expected outcome: External concentrate pathways are secure, unobstructed, and properly supplied.

steps.title: 5. Verify Water Preparation Is Normal
steps.instructions: Confirm the machine has completed its normal water-preparation process without unresolved alarms. Review whether any recent water inlet or integrated purification problems occurred. Conductivity instability associated with a water-preparation problem should be addressed as a water-system issue before further dialysis troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Water preparation is stable and no unresolved water-related condition is present.

steps.title: 6. Check Setup and Configuration
steps.instructions: Verify the selected treatment setup and accessible parameters are appropriate for the intended therapy and have not been accidentally changed. Do not alter restricted calibration or service parameters. Expected outcome: The machine is configured for the intended treatment without unintended user-level setup changes.

steps.title: 7. Replace Questionable External Supplies With Known-Good Supplies
steps.instructions: If a concentrate container, connector, or disposable is suspect, replace it with an approved known-good equivalent when permitted by facility procedure. Change one variable at a time so the corrective action can be identified. Expected outcome: Conductivity stabilizes with the known-good supply if the original external component caused the problem. Troubleshooting can stop after successful verification.

steps.title: 8. Repeat the Preparation Sequence
steps.instructions: With the machine off patient, repeat the normal preparation process and observe whether conductivity reaches and maintains the system's accepted condition. Do not bypass or silence recurring safety checks merely to advance the setup. Expected outcome: Conductivity stabilizes and remains accepted by the system. If so, continue to final verification.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm the Tablo completes pre-treatment preparation without conductivity alarms and maintains stable dialysate preparation through the normal verification period. Expected outcome: No recurrent conductivity alarm occurs and the machine reaches the expected ready state. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Conductivity Instability
steps.instructions: If correct concentrates, proper connections, normal water preparation, and appropriate setup are confirmed but conductivity remains unstable, remove the device from service. Expected outcome: Internal proportioning, sensing, fluid-control, or calibration-related causes are left to qualified service evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Dialysis staff reported the Tablo would not stabilize conductivity during treatment preparation.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the concentrate connection was not completely seated, resulting in inconsistent concentrate delivery.
CCR.Resolution: Reseated the approved concentrate connection, repeated preparation, verified stable conductivity with no recurring alarm, and returned the unit to service.

title: Outset Medical Tablo Hemodialysis (HD) Machine - Dialysate Temperature Out of Range
description: Troubleshoot dialysate temperature problems caused by water conditions, setup, airflow, environment, or external operating conditions before qualified service evaluation.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient
steps.instructions: Do not initiate or continue dialysis with an unresolved dialysate temperature alarm or unreliable temperature control. If the condition occurs during treatment, follow the facility's clinical procedure for safely maintaining or transferring therapy. Do not defeat a temperature-related safety alarm. Expected outcome: The patient is protected from potentially unsafe dialysate temperature and troubleshooting occurs off patient.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Temperature Problem
steps.instructions: Determine whether the reported condition is: Temperature too high Temperature too low Temperature fluctuating Excessive warm-up time Failure to stabilize during preparation A temperature message that appears only intermittently Record the exact message and when it occurs. Expected outcome: The symptom and timing are clearly defined.

steps.title: 3. Verify Normal Water Preparation
steps.instructions: Confirm the machine has completed its water-preparation process normally and has no unresolved water inlet or purification problem. An abnormal or interrupted water supply may affect downstream dialysate preparation. Expected outcome: Water preparation is functioning normally before temperature control is evaluated further.

steps.title: 4. Verify Treatment Settings
steps.instructions: Review user-accessible treatment settings to ensure the intended temperature-related selections have not been accidentally changed. Do not enter service menus or adjust calibration values. Expected outcome: The accessible treatment configuration matches the intended clinical setup.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Ventilation and Ambient Conditions
steps.instructions: Check that ventilation openings are unobstructed and the Tablo is not positioned against objects that restrict airflow. Look for excessive room heat, direct heat sources, unusually cold conditions, or recent relocation. Expected outcome: The machine has adequate airflow and is operating in a normal clinical environment. If correcting the environment resolves the condition, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 6. Inspect External Fluid Connections
steps.instructions: Check accessible water, drain, concentrate, and disposable fluid connections for kinks, restrictions, poor seating, or other conditions that could interfere with normal fluid preparation. Expected outcome: External fluid paths are correctly connected and unobstructed.

steps.title: 7. Allow a Normal Preparation Cycle
steps.instructions: With the machine off patient, perform its normal preparation sequence and observe whether temperature reaches the system's accepted condition without recurring alarms. Do not repeatedly reset an alarm that immediately returns. Expected outcome: Dialysate temperature stabilizes normally and the system proceeds through setup. If successful, continue to final verification.

steps.title: 8. Compare Behavior After Correcting External Conditions
steps.instructions: If an obvious environmental or connection problem was corrected, repeat preparation from a normal starting condition. Avoid making multiple simultaneous changes that obscure the cause. Expected outcome: The temperature-related issue does not recur after correction.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Verify the machine completes preparation and remains free of temperature alarms through the normal pre-treatment verification process. Expected outcome: Temperature control is stable and accepted by the machine. Troubleshooting can stop and return-to-service procedures may be completed.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Temperature Failure
steps.instructions: If normal water preparation, configuration, connections, ventilation, and environmental conditions are confirmed but temperature remains abnormal, remove the machine from service. Expected outcome: Heating, sensing, fluid-control, or other internal temperature-control problems are evaluated by qualified service personnel.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported the Tablo repeatedly stopped during preparation because dialysate temperature would not stabilize.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the unit positioned with its ventilation openings obstructed by stored supplies.
CCR.Resolution: Cleared the ventilation area, repeated preparation successfully, verified stable operation without a recurring temperature alarm, and returned the unit to service.

helpfulDetails: Point in setup where it occurred

title: Outset Medical Tablo Hemodialysis (HD) Machine - Blood Leak Detector Alarm or Detector Test Failure
description: Troubleshoot blood leak detector alarms or test failures caused by disposable setup, contamination, bubbles, fluid conditions, or detector-area problems before escalation.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient
steps.instructions: Treat a blood leak alarm during dialysis as clinically significant until a true blood leak has been excluded through the appropriate clinical process. Do not continue treatment based solely on an assumption that the detector is faulty. If the alarm occurs during treatment, clinical staff must manage the patient and extracorporeal circuit according to facility procedure before Clinical Engineering troubleshooting begins. Expected outcome: The patient and blood circuit are managed safely, and technical troubleshooting occurs only after the device is removed from active patient dependence.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Complaint
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem is: A blood leak alarm during treatment A detector test that will not pass A repeated alarm during preparation An intermittent alarm A problem associated with one disposable setup Record the exact displayed message and timing. Expected outcome: The detector issue is clearly characterized.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Disposable Fluid Path
steps.instructions: With the system safely off patient, inspect the relevant disposable fluid path for: Incorrect installation Kinks Poor seating Abnormal fluid appearance Air or foam Visible contamination Damage Do not reuse a questionable disposable simply to test the machine. Expected outcome: The disposable pathway is installed correctly and appears normal. If correcting installation resolves the detector test, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Accessible Detector Area
steps.instructions: Inspect the externally accessible detector area for contamination, moisture, residue, discoloration, or an improperly seated disposable segment. Clean only according to approved cleaning procedures. Do not insert tools or disassemble the detector. Expected outcome: The detector area is clean, dry, unobstructed, and the disposable is correctly positioned.

steps.title: 5. Check for Air, Foam, or Abnormal Fluid Conditions
steps.instructions: Air, foam, or unusual fluid conditions may interfere with optical sensing. Confirm the normal preparation sequence has completed and that the fluid path does not contain an obvious abnormality. Expected outcome: The fluid presented to the detector is appropriate for the normal detector test.

steps.title: 6. Substitute a Known-Good Disposable When Appropriate
steps.instructions: If the installed disposable is suspect, replace it with a new approved disposable according to facility practice and repeat setup. Change only one variable at a time. Expected outcome: The blood leak detector test passes with the replacement disposable if the original setup caused the problem.

steps.title: 7. Repeat the Normal Detector Test
steps.instructions: Run only the normal user-accessible preparation or detector verification sequence. Do not bypass, disable, recalibrate, or alter detector thresholds through unauthorized menus. Expected outcome: The detector test passes and no alarm recurs. If successful, continue to final functional verification.

steps.title: 8. Check for Recurrence
steps.instructions: Allow the machine to complete the relevant preparation process and verify that the detector remains stable. Expected outcome: No repeated blood leak detector warning or failed test occurs.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm all normal pre-treatment checks complete successfully and there is no unresolved blood leak detector condition. Expected outcome: The Tablo passes its required preparation checks and is ready for service according to facility procedure. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Repeated Detector Failure
steps.instructions: If the detector area is clean, the disposable is correct, and the test repeatedly fails, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The machine is removed from service for qualified evaluation of the detector or associated internal systems.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported the Tablo repeatedly failed the blood leak detector check during setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found residue on the accessible detector area preventing reliable optical sensing.
CCR.Resolution: Cleaned and dried the detector area using the approved procedure, installed the disposable correctly, repeated setup successfully, and verified the detector test passed before return to service.

helpfulDetails: Exact blood leak alarm or message

title: Outset Medical Tablo Hemodialysis (HD) Machine - Air Detector Alarm or Venous Clamp Problem
description: Troubleshoot air detection and venous clamp problems caused by tubing placement, air, disposable setup, obstruction, contamination, or clamp-area issues.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient
steps.instructions: An air detector alarm or unreliable venous clamp is a patient-safety issue. Do not troubleshoot the detector or clamp while the patient relies on the machine's blood-return safety functions. If the issue occurs during treatment, clinical staff must manage the blood circuit and patient according to facility procedure before technical troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Patient safety is maintained and the device is removed from active treatment before technical evaluation.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Condition
steps.instructions: Determine whether the machine has: Detected air Failed an air detector check Failed to recognize tubing Closed the venous clamp unexpectedly Failed to close or release the clamp Produced an intermittent alarm Record the exact message and whether the problem occurs during setup or treatment. Expected outcome: The complaint is clearly defined and reproducible.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Blood Tubing and Disposable Setup
steps.instructions: With the machine off patient, inspect the relevant blood tubing for: Air Loose connections Incorrect routing Kinks Flattening Damage Incorrect installation in the detector or clamp Do not bypass the air detector or clamp. Expected outcome: Tubing is properly routed and seated with no obvious air or physical defect. If correcting tubing placement resolves the issue, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Air Detector Area
steps.instructions: Check the accessible detector surface and tubing channel for moisture, residue, contamination, or obstruction. Clean only with the approved method and ensure the area is dry before retesting. Expected outcome: The detector area is clean and the tubing is positioned correctly.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Venous Clamp Area
steps.instructions: With no patient connected, visually inspect the accessible clamp mechanism for: Tubing incorrectly placed Obstruction Dried residue Visible damage Foreign material preventing movement Do not force the clamp open or closed. Expected outcome: The clamp pathway is unobstructed and the tubing can be installed normally.

steps.title: 6. Replace Questionable Tubing or Disposable Components
steps.instructions: If the tubing is stretched, damaged, deformed, contaminated, or otherwise suspect, install a new approved disposable set according to normal setup procedure. Expected outcome: The air detector and clamp operate normally with the known-good disposable if the original setup was responsible.

steps.title: 7. Repeat the Normal Setup Check
steps.instructions: Run the machine's normal user-accessible setup sequence and observe air detector and clamp behavior. Do not enter service menus or bypass the safety test. Expected outcome: The air detector passes its normal check and the venous clamp actuates as expected without recurring alarms.

steps.title: 8. Check for Intermittent Mechanical Behavior
steps.instructions: Observe the clamp through several normal machine-controlled operations during the permitted setup process. Do not manually manipulate it beyond normal external interaction. Expected outcome: Clamp movement is consistent, complete, and repeatable.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Verify that normal pre-treatment checks complete successfully and that no air detector or venous clamp fault remains. Expected outcome: Both safety functions operate normally through setup. Troubleshooting can stop and the machine may be returned to service according to facility policy.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Safety-System Failure
steps.instructions: If correct tubing placement, a clean detector/clamp area, and a known-good disposable do not resolve the problem, remove the machine from service. Expected outcome: Internal detector, clamp actuator, sensing, control, or calibration problems are referred for qualified service.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported the Tablo failed its air detection check and the venous line clamp remained engaged during setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the venous tubing was not fully seated in the designated detector and clamp pathway.
CCR.Resolution: Corrected tubing placement, repeated setup successfully, verified normal air detection and clamp operation, and returned the machine to service.

title: Outset Medical Tablo Hemodialysis (HD) Machine - Arterial or Venous Pressure Reading Incorrect or Unstable
description: Troubleshoot inaccurate or unstable arterial or venous pressure readings caused by tubing, pressure connections, air, clamping, disposable setup, or patient-circuit conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient
steps.instructions: Do not rely on unstable or clearly incorrect arterial or venous pressure monitoring during dialysis. If the issue occurs during treatment, clinical staff should assess the patient and extracorporeal circuit and follow facility procedure for safely stopping or transferring treatment when required. Technical troubleshooting should occur off patient whenever device performance is uncertain. Expected outcome: The patient is not dependent on unreliable pressure monitoring during troubleshooting.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Pressure Channel Is Affected
steps.instructions: Determine whether the issue involves: Arterial pressure Venous pressure Both channels A fixed or implausible reading Excessive fluctuation A reading that changes with tubing movement A problem appearing only during pump operation Record the exact reported behavior. Expected outcome: The affected channel and failure pattern are identified.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Extracorporeal Tubing Setup
steps.instructions: With the machine off patient, inspect the blood tubing and pressure-monitoring portions of the disposable setup for: Kinks Clamps left closed Twisted tubing Loose connections Incorrect routing Collapsed segments Visible damage Expected outcome: The tubing path is installed correctly and free of obvious restrictions. If correcting an external setup issue stabilizes pressure readings, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Pressure Connections and Interfaces
steps.instructions: Check accessible pressure interfaces and connections for secure seating, contamination, moisture, loose fittings, or incorrectly installed disposable components. Do not open internal pressure-sensing assemblies. Expected outcome: Pressure interfaces are clean, dry, properly connected, and mechanically secure.

steps.title: 5. Check for Air or Fluid Where It Should Not Be
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible pressure-monitoring portions of the circuit for abnormal air or fluid conditions that may interfere with pressure transmission. Use normal setup procedures only; do not improvise purging or pressure-source methods. Expected outcome: The disposable pressure-monitoring path is in the expected setup condition.

steps.title: 6. Replace the Suspect Disposable
steps.instructions: If the tubing or pressure interface remains questionable, replace the disposable set with a new approved set and repeat setup. This is particularly useful when a problem follows one specific tubing set. Expected outcome: Stable pressure behavior with the replacement disposable indicates the original disposable or setup caused the condition.

steps.title: 7. Observe Pressure Behavior During Normal Off-Patient Testing
steps.instructions: Use the normal machine preparation or approved functional test process to observe whether the affected reading responds consistently. Do not apply unapproved pressure sources or enter unauthorized calibration functions. Expected outcome: Pressure readings behave consistently and no longer fluctuate abnormally.

steps.title: 8. Check Related Pump and Clamp Conditions
steps.instructions: Confirm there is no simultaneous blood-pump, tubing, or clamp problem that could account for abnormal pressure behavior. A pressure alarm may be the result of an actual flow restriction rather than a failed pressure sensor. Expected outcome: Other external components that influence circuit pressure are operating normally.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Complete the normal pre-treatment verification sequence and confirm arterial and venous pressure monitoring is stable with the approved setup. Expected outcome: Both pressure channels operate consistently with no unexplained alarm or instability. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Pressure-Monitoring Problems
steps.instructions: If the disposable, pressure connections, tubing path, and related external conditions are satisfactory but readings remain unreliable, remove the machine from service. Expected outcome: Internal sensing, pneumatic interface, signal processing, calibration, or other service-level problems are referred for qualified evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported the Tablo displayed an unstable venous pressure value that changed significantly with minor tubing movement.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the venous pressure connection on the disposable was incompletely seated.
CCR.Resolution: Installed the pressure connection correctly, repeated setup, verified stable arterial and venous pressure monitoring, and returned the machine to service.

helpfulDetails: Arterial, venous, or both channels affected
Whether condition occurred with pump running
Presence of air or fluid abnormality

title: Outset Medical Tablo Hemodialysis (HD) Machine - Blood Pump Will Not Run or Speed Is Inconsistent
description: Troubleshoot blood-pump failure or unstable speed caused by tubing installation, obstruction, controls, disposable setup, alarms, or external mechanical interference.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient
steps.instructions: Do not continue dialysis with a blood pump that stops unexpectedly or runs inconsistently. If the issue occurs during treatment, clinical staff should manage the extracorporeal circuit and patient according to facility procedure before Clinical Engineering evaluation. Do not repeatedly restart an unreliable blood pump on a patient. Expected outcome: Patient therapy is safely maintained or transferred and the affected machine is available for off-patient troubleshooting.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Pump Complaint
steps.instructions: Determine whether the pump: Does not start Starts and immediately stops Runs intermittently Appears unusually slow or fast Changes speed unexpectedly Produces abnormal sound or vibration Stops because another alarm condition is active Expected outcome: The pump problem is differentiated from a machine safety interlock or unrelated alarm.

steps.title: 3. Check for Active Alarms or Interlocks
steps.instructions: Review the normal user display for other conditions that intentionally prevent blood-pump operation, such as an unresolved setup or safety alarm. Do not bypass an alarm simply to force the pump to run. Expected outcome: Any legitimate external reason for inhibited pump operation is identified and corrected first.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Blood Tubing Installation
steps.instructions: With no patient connected, inspect the pump tubing segment for: Correct routing Full seating Twisting Kinks Excessive stretching Flattening Visible damage Incorrect disposable installation Expected outcome: Pump tubing is correctly installed and free of mechanical obstruction. If correcting tubing placement restores normal pump operation, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Accessible Pump Area
steps.instructions: Check for dried residue, foreign material, damaged tubing fragments, or another external obstruction around the accessible pump mechanism. Do not disassemble the pump or force rollers or drive components manually. Expected outcome: The accessible pump path is clean and unobstructed.

steps.title: 6. Install a Known-Good Approved Disposable
steps.instructions: If the tubing segment is suspect, replace the disposable set with a new approved set and repeat the normal setup process. Expected outcome: Normal pump operation with the replacement disposable indicates the original tubing or setup caused the issue.

steps.title: 7. Verify User Controls and Programmed Conditions
steps.instructions: Confirm user-accessible pump-related settings are appropriate and controls respond normally. Determine whether a touchscreen or control-input problem is preventing commands from being accepted. Do not modify service-level motor parameters. Expected outcome: Pump commands are accepted normally and no user-level configuration issue is present.

steps.title: 8. Observe Pump Operation Off Patient
steps.instructions: Using the normal approved setup process, observe pump start, stop, and speed stability. Listen for unusual grinding, clicking, binding, or other abnormal mechanical sound. Expected outcome: The pump operates smoothly and consistently without unintended speed changes or abnormal noise.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Allow the Tablo to complete its normal preparation and applicable pump checks with the approved disposable installed. Expected outcome: Blood-pump operation is consistent and no recurring pump-related alarm is present. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Pump Failure
steps.instructions: If proper tubing, clean external pump surfaces, known-good disposables, and correct controls have been verified but the pump remains unreliable, remove the machine from service. Expected outcome: Motor, drive, sensing, control, or other internal pump-related faults are evaluated by qualified service personnel.

CCR.Complaint: Dialysis staff reported the Tablo blood pump would start and then stop during setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the pump tubing segment twisted and not fully seated in the pump pathway.
CCR.Resolution: Corrected the tubing installation, repeated setup, verified smooth and stable blood-pump operation, and returned the machine to service.

helpfulDetails: Pump would not start or ran inconsistently

title: Outset Medical Tablo Hemodialysis (HD) Machine - Treatment Data Will Not Upload or Network Connection Is Lost
description: Troubleshoot treatment-data upload and connectivity problems caused by network availability, configuration, signal, infrastructure, or communication-path interruptions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Preserve the Clinical Record
steps.instructions: A network problem should not distract from safe dialysis treatment. Do not interrupt functioning therapy solely to troubleshoot data connectivity unless clinical workflow requires it. Ensure required treatment information is preserved or documented using the facility's approved downtime process when electronic transfer is unavailable. Expected outcome: Patient care continues safely and required treatment documentation is not lost because of the network issue.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Connectivity Problem
steps.instructions: Determine whether the Tablo: Shows no network connection Loses connection intermittently Connects but treatment data does not upload Uploads some treatments but not others Cannot reach the expected destination Developed the problem after relocation or infrastructure changes Record any displayed network or upload message. Expected outcome: The problem is separated into device connectivity versus data-transfer failure.

steps.title: 3. Check the Device's Normal Network Status
steps.instructions: Review user-accessible network status indicators without changing protected configuration. Note whether the machine appears connected, disconnected, or intermittently connected. Expected outcome: The current connectivity state is documented. If the device reconnects and pending data transfers normally, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Accessible Network Connections
steps.instructions: If the installation uses accessible physical connections, inspect them for looseness, damage, contamination, or strain. If communication is wireless, confirm the machine is located where the approved network is expected to be available. Do not connect the device to an unapproved network. Expected outcome: The external communication path is physically intact and appropriate for the installation.

steps.title: 5. Compare With Other Devices or Locations
steps.instructions: Determine whether other Tablo systems or approved networked equipment in the same area are also affected. If multiple devices lose connectivity simultaneously, involve the appropriate IT or network support team before assuming a Tablo hardware problem. Expected outcome: The issue is narrowed to the individual machine or shared network infrastructure.

steps.title: 6. Check for Recent Infrastructure or Location Changes
steps.instructions: Ask whether the device was recently moved, the network was changed, maintenance occurred, credentials or certificates were updated, or a clinical interface experienced downtime. Avoid making undocumented network configuration changes. Expected outcome: Any infrastructure-related change associated with the onset of the problem is identified.

steps.title: 7. Perform a Normal Reconnection or Restart When Appropriate
steps.instructions: When the machine is not supporting a patient and normal workflow permits it, use standard user-accessible controls to reconnect or perform a controlled restart. Do not repeatedly reboot an active treatment system just to restore data transfer. Expected outcome: The device reconnects and normal data transmission resumes. If it does, verify successful upload before stopping troubleshooting.

steps.title: 8. Verify the Complete Data Path
steps.instructions: Confirm not only that the device indicates connectivity, but also that the expected treatment data reaches its intended clinical destination when a valid test or completed record is available. Coordinate with IT or application support when the device is connected but the receiving system does not show the record. Expected outcome: The complete communication path is confirmed from the Tablo to the intended receiving system.

steps.title: 9. Document Any Downtime or Delayed Upload
steps.instructions: If data transfer was delayed, confirm clinical staff have followed appropriate documentation procedures and that records are reconciled after connectivity returns. Expected outcome: No required treatment documentation is omitted because of the outage.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Connectivity Failure
steps.instructions: If accessible connections, device status, location, and facility network availability appear normal but the Tablo cannot maintain communication or upload records, escalate appropriately. Expected outcome: Device-level communication, configuration, application, security, or infrastructure causes are investigated by qualified technical teams.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported the Tablo completed treatments normally but treatment records were no longer uploading to the expected system.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the device had lost its approved network connection after being moved to a different treatment area.
CCR.Resolution: Returned the unit to the approved connected location, verified network connectivity and successful treatment-data transfer, and confirmed normal operation with staff.

helpfulDetails: Whether treatment data is retained locally

title: Outset Medical Tablo Hemodialysis (HD) Machine - Disinfection or Rinse Cycle Will Not Complete
description: Troubleshoot incomplete disinfection or rinse cycles caused by water, drain, consumables, connections, setup, interruptions, or environmental conditions before service escalation.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Prevent Premature Reuse
steps.instructions: Do not place a Tablo into clinical service when the required disinfection or rinse process has not completed successfully. Clearly identify the machine as unavailable until the cycle is completed and verified. Expected outcome: No patient is connected to a machine with incomplete or uncertain disinfection status.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Where the Cycle Fails
steps.instructions: Determine whether the machine: Will not start the cycle Stops early Pauses or stalls at a repeatable stage Fails during rinse Repeats part of the cycle Displays a specific disinfection-related message Loses power or water during the process Record the exact displayed wording and cycle stage. Expected outcome: The failure is clearly characterized and reproducible.

steps.title: 3. Verify AC Power
steps.instructions: Confirm the machine has stable facility AC power and that the power cord and receptacle are secure and undamaged. A long cleaning or disinfection process may expose intermittent power problems not obvious during brief operation. Expected outcome: Stable power is available throughout the process. If restoring reliable power allows the cycle to complete, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Verify Water Supply
steps.instructions: Inspect the approved water connection, inlet hose, and accessible valve for secure connection, kinks, restriction, damage, or leakage. Confirm there has not been a building water interruption. Expected outcome: Adequate external water supply is available for the complete cycle.

steps.title: 5. Verify Drainage
steps.instructions: Check the drain hose and drain location for: Kinks Blockage Improper positioning Backup Disconnection Visible leakage Do not attempt internal drain-system disassembly. Expected outcome: The machine can discharge wastewater normally. If correcting an external drain restriction permits cycle completion, the issue is resolved.

steps.title: 6. Verify Required Consumables or Chemistry
steps.instructions: If the selected process requires approved consumables or chemistry, confirm the correct item is present, properly installed, not visibly damaged, and appropriately recognized through the normal user workflow. Do not substitute unapproved chemistry or bypass recognition checks. Expected outcome: Required supplies are correct and properly installed.

steps.title: 7. Inspect Accessible Fluid Connections
steps.instructions: Check external fluid connections and disposable interfaces for incomplete seating, kinks, leaks, or other obvious abnormalities that could interrupt circulation or rinsing. Expected outcome: External fluid pathways are correctly connected and free of obvious restriction.

steps.title: 8. Repeat the Normal Cycle When Appropriate
steps.instructions: After correcting any external issue, start the normal disinfection or rinse process from the appropriate user-accessible workflow. Do not repeatedly restart a failing cycle without addressing the cause, and do not bypass required cycle stages. Expected outcome: The complete disinfection or rinse cycle proceeds without interruption.

steps.title: 9. Verify Successful Completion
steps.instructions: Confirm the machine indicates the process completed successfully and reaches the expected post-cycle state. Check for remaining alarms, visible leaks, or unresolved rinse status. Do not assume the cycle completed merely because the machine stopped running. Expected outcome: The full required process completes successfully with no unresolved condition. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate a Repeated Cycle Failure
steps.instructions: If stable power, water supply, drainage, required consumables, and external connections are verified but the cycle repeatedly fails, remove the device from service. Expected outcome: Internal fluid-control, heating, sensing, purification, software, or related service-level problems are referred for qualified evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Dialysis staff reported the Tablo repeatedly stopped before completing its rinse cycle.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external drain hose pinched behind the machine, restricting wastewater flow.
CCR.Resolution: Corrected the drain hose routing, repeated the rinse cycle to successful completion, verified no leaks or recurring alarms, and returned the unit to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether the failure repeats at the same stage
